_comment: THE ONE PLACE the plugin's identity lives. Everything that carries it — .claude-plugin/plugin.json, .codex-plugin/plugin.json, .antigravity-plugin/plugin.json, the generated mcp_config.json and hooks.json, the 92 permission rules in skills/soc-investigate/settings.snippet.json and the identity.sh include that install.sh/preflight.sh source — is GENERATED from this file by gen_identity.py; CI fails if they drift. To re-brand or re-key the plugin (e.g. a vendor catalog shipping it under its own name), change `name`/`displayName`/`description` here and run `python3 plugin/gen_identity.py`. The optional `distribution` block holds everything that is per-COPY rather than per-plugin, and it has two halves that do different things. The terms half (`license`, `homepage`, `repository`, plus the prose keys `vendor`, `terms`, `support`, `antigravityInstall`) says this copy is redistributed under someone else's terms: the manifests take those values, the distribution-only prose is filled from them ({{vendor}}, {{terms}}, {{support}}, {{antigravity_install}}) and the community-only/distribution-only prose switches. The listing half (`documentationUrl`, `supportUrl`, `privacyPolicyUrl`, `termsOfServiceUrl`) only describes a directory ENTRY, is emitted into the Claude manifest alone, and does NOT switch the prose — so this repo can carry its own listing without its docs calling it a redistribution. Those four must be https:// with a host. The top-level `license` stays the software's and keeps driving the SPDX headers, README badge and identity.sh. `name` is load-bearing: it is the Claude Code plugin key and the skill/MCP namespace prefix (`<name>:<skill>`, `mcp__plugin_<name>_<server>__<tool>`) that the permission gate matches on. `displayName`, `logo` and `suggestedPrompts` are what the Antigravity listing needs — a distribution overrides them here, including `logo`, so the listing carries its own mark. That manifest accepts ONLY name/displayName/version/description/logo/suggestedPrompts/disabled and silently drops anything else, so `keywords` and `category` reach the other two hosts only. `shortDescription` is the listing's description on Antigravity and Codex: Google recommends 120–160 characters, and it must not promise a prompt that the host controls rather than this plugin — the gate itself runs on all three hosts (hooks/hooks.json on Claude Code, hooks.json on Antigravity, the approval policy on Codex). `mcpServer` must equal permissions.json's `server` and the server key in .mcp.json/.mcp.codex.json; the generator refuses to run when they disagree.
name: raffkin
shortDescription: Triage Exabeam New-Scale alerts and cases end to end: gather the evidence, map MITRE, reach a verdict, and record it behind an approval step.
description: Raffkin — agentic SOC analyst skill suite. Investigates and triages Exabeam New-Scale alerts and cases through the Exabeam MCP: evidence gathering, entity pivots, threat/false-positive verdict, and action — with containment recommended for human approval and dismiss/close gated by the host agent's tool-approval rules.
suggestedPrompts: Triage my open Exabeam cases and tell me what to look at first
Investigate the highest-risk Exabeam alert from the last 24 hours and give me a verdict
Find the noisiest Exabeam detection rules and propose tuning
